title: Audit ingest: index lifecycle, coldstore spill, and emergency retention throttle
creator: Marisol Chen
description:
Background:
We continue to see unpredictable storage growth spikes from long-tail audit events and large batched exports. Current strategy (time-based daily indices kept in hot store) is simple but expensive for low-query older data. This ticket defines an index lifecycle (ILM)-style policy that moves older audit indices to a coldstore (object blob) via a controlled spill process, and an emergency retention throttle that constrains ingest when projected storage spend exceeds budget thresholds. It also locks retention and throttle controls behind RBAC v2 admin roles and SSO/SAML enforced groups.

Goals:
- Reduce persistent hot storage by at least 45% for audit indices older than 30 days while keeping 30-day query latency SLOs.
- Ensure we can restore coldstore indices for ad-hoc investigations within 2 hours (on-demand restore path).
- Prevent runaway cost during incident spikes via emergency retention throttle that limits ingestion rate per-org and globally when thresholds are hit.
- Make retention/eviction controls auditable and only editable by RBAC v2 admins (SSO groups: security-admins, infra-admins).

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Index lifecycle policies: implement ILM rules with three states - hot (30d), warm (30-90d, optimized index for search), and coldspill (>90d) where segment files are snapshotted into object storage (S3) and index metadata is replaced with a lightweight stub.
2) Coldstore spill: create a spill worker that packages index segments into compressed blobs, uploads to object store, and replaces index shards with a pointer. Query layer will transparently trigger a fetch/restore for shards referenced by pointer; restore prioritization respects SLAs.
3) Emergency retention throttle: a control plane evaluator computes projected 7-day storage spend based on current ingest rate and historical size-per-event; when surpassing budget thresholds, throttle circuits apply backpressure at ingress (token bucket per-tenant + global throttle). Throttle settings are adjustable by RBAC v2 admins only and leave a read-only audit history.
4) RBAC/SSO integration: extend RBAC v2 to include retention-policy roles and an immutable audit trail for changes. Admin console endpoints protected by SAML groups and logged to audit pipeline (separate immutable index).
5) Metrics/observability: add Grafana dashboards and alerts for bytes/day, projected spend, coldstore spill throughput, restore latency, and throttle activation rate.

Trade-offs considered:
- Per-tenant partitioning vs global time-based lifecycle: per-tenant gives better isolation but is operationally heavy; we chose time-based with per-tenant throttle hooks to balance complexity and cost.
- Full immediate restore vs staged fetch-on-demand: immediate restore preserves latency but is costly; we prefer staged fetch-with-prioritization to meet cost targets while achieving a 2h target for analyst restores.
- Aggressive index compression vs coldstore spill: compression alone was insufficient for >45% reduction; combining both gives headroom for future growth.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated spill run completes for a 60-day-old index within expected window and reduces hot storage footprint by >40% in canary tenant.
- Emergency throttle activates during a synthetic 3x ingest storm and holds projected spend under configured budget while maintaining graceful degradation documented in runbook.
- RBAC-protected retention settings cannot be modified by non-admins; all changes are recorded in audit-index with timestamp and actor.
- Restore flow validated with a sub-2h median time for ad-hoc index restores in staging.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement ILM + mock spill pipeline for single canary org; monitor for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2: enable actual coldstore spills for canary orgs and add restore worker; run soak testing.
- Phase 3: enable emergency throttle gates in a read-only mode (monitor-only) for a week before switching to enforce.
- Phase 4: gradual opt-in rollout per org tied to customer communications and release notes.
